candidates.name: A. The verification bench (instrument dark, signal labels)
candidates.product: A free, long-form SystemVerilog, UVM and AMBA verification course: 112 lessons in four tiers with interactives, labs and interview prep, for engineers from their first testbench to staff-level interviews, with progress kept in the learner's own browser.
candidates.world: A verification engineer's bench during a regression run: the waveform viewer with named signals and a time cursor, the simulator log, the LRM open in a second window. Near-graphite instrument surfaces, with colour only where a signal or a state needs it.
candidates.moments: 1) Inside lessons and practice: the interactives and diagrams (scheduler region ladder, UVM phase lanes, cost ladder, module map) keep their full semantic palette and are the only rich colour on those screens. 2) On the landing page: the hero's static scheduler frame. On the curriculum index: the M0 to M8 milestone ladder drawn as one rung line. The ladder is not added to the landing page, because that would add a section.
candidates.signature: The signal-name tag: every module code, milestone ID and lesson reference (F1A, I-UVM-1C, M3, B-APB-1) set as one small mono label (12/16 JetBrains Mono, radius 4, 8% hairline, muted text), like the signal names in a waveform viewer's left column. One SignalTag component used in the outline, breadcrumbs, lesson eyebrow, 'Before you start', 'Builds toward', LearnInLesson, ModuleCard, the ladder and Resources 'Used in', and nowhere else.
candidates.neutrals: Dark (default): deepest #0e0f12, page #131418, card #191a1f, raised #22242a, hairline = primary text at 8%. Text #eceef2 / #a2a7b3 / #80858f (muted is about 5:1 on the page). The deepest surface is the single code-surface token (pre, Monaco editor.background, traces). Light: page #f8f8f7, card #ffffff, raised #f1f1f0, text #17181b / #50535a / #70737a, shadow 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.05). Surfaces never carry the accent hue.
candidates.accent: Signal sky, tamed from the existing #00BFFF: #3cc2ef on dark (a fill with #0e0f12 text, about 9:1) and #0a6c9e on light (ink and fill with white text, about 5.5:1). Used for one primary action per screen, a 2px current-row marker, the active TOC entry and focus. Mint is retired. On dark the hero primary may be off-white #eceef2 with dark text. Semantic colours stay, toned to the ramp: positive #4cc38a / #16a34a, negative #e5484d / #dc2626, warning amber. The phase-map and scheduler region hues live only inside the moments.
candidates.type: From the tokens' 'Precise, technical, calm' row. IBM Plex Sans 400 and 500 (600 rarely) for interface and long reading, with JetBrains Mono (already loaded, ligatures off) for code, signal tags, counts and keycaps. Both are free under OFL. Interface 14-15/20-22, lesson body 16-17/28 at about 70ch, H1 32-36/1.15 at 500, h2 24/32, h3 18-20/28, landing hero 56-64 at 500 with -0.03em (40 on mobile). Cal Sans is removed. Inter is the zero-new-files fallback (already loaded at 400; needs a 500 file).
candidates.darkAndLight: One brand in two lighting conditions: same structure, radii, type and signature, with the ramp inverted and the same accent hue (lighter fill on dark, deeper ink on light). All ten themes keep their ids (default, ocean, sunset, forest and violet, each light and dark), so stored preferences and tests survive. Only the values change: every theme uses the shared ramps, and each palette swaps --primary and --ring for a dark fill shade and a light ink shade that both pass 4.5:1. Semantic visual colours read the same in every theme. The palette picker moves to /settings or the light/dark button's popover. Dark stays the default.
candidates.hero: An asymmetric split on the plain page surface. Left: the headline in the product's nouns (for example 'SystemVerilog, UVM and AMBA verification, from your first testbench to staff-level interviews'), a fixed factual subhead (112 lessons in four tiers, with interactives, labs and interview prep; progress stays in this browser), then 'Find your level' (primary) and 'Browse the curriculum' (secondary). Right, at least 50% of the width: a static frame composed from existing parts. RegionLadder (src/components/visuals/scheduler/RegionLadder.tsx), the nine-region ladder from Preponed to Postponed with the current region marked, sits above StepWaveform (src/components/visual-system/StepWaveform.tsx). CodeTrace (src/components/visual-system/CodeTrace.tsx) shows the two always blocks. The data comes from simulateTimeSlot in src/lib/sv-scheduler-model.ts on the 'shift-blocking' and 'shift-nba' scenarios from src/lib/sv-scheduler-scenarios.ts, frozen at one step, so '=' versus '<=' is visible. It does not embed the full TimeSlotTraceVisualizer, which brings PredictionPrompt, PlaybackControls and SegmentedControl. It sits inside one window on the deepest surface with a hairline. All three parts are already client components, like HeroSection. An optional quiet top bar is the owner's call.
candidates.risks: 1) A near-graphite dark can slide into the template look. The signal tags, the hero frame and the ladder must be built with care. 2) Sky in the chrome sits near the phase map's sky function-phase colour, so keep the chrome accent sparse and check it beside phase diagrams. 3) Plex Sans changes wrapping across 112 lessons, the TOC and the outline. There are no Playwright screenshot baselines (no toHaveScreenshot in tests/), but text-pinned tests break (see tests). 4) Violet-dark users lose purple surfaces. 5) Plex needs two new woff2 files on a disk-tight machine; Inter avoids that. 6) Sentence-casing the module titles and lesson section names is a content change: the slugs stay, the tests change.

direction.recommended: A. The verification bench (instrument dark, signal labels)
direction.reason: A comes from what learners do: verification engineers who live in waveform viewers, logs and editors on dark screens, which matches the dark default without tinting the surfaces. It keeps semantic colour intact (red fail, green pass, amber task phase and warning, region hues inside the moments), whereas B's red accent collides with fail. Its single signature already half-exists in the outline's mono codes and LearnInLesson keycaps. Its hero is built only from existing components (RegionLadder, StepWaveform, CodeTrace, sv-scheduler-model), so it shows something true with no image tool. The neutral ramps plus accent swaps make every interactive read reliably across all ten themes while keeping their ids.
